turns.content: omg okay so i’m literally sitting in my car right now outside the plant and it’s 1:25 💀 cutover is at 2. ray refused to hand over the diagnostic logs until i “ask nicely.” i walked out. now i’m spiraling—was that completely unprofessional or was i right to draw a hard line?? tbh i have the remote admin app open and i could lock his station from here. should i do it?? like protect the cutover or is that too nuclear?? 😭
That’s a lot to be sitting with in a parking lot with 35 minutes on the clock. Checking whether we’ve talked about this cutover or Ray before so the advice actually fits.

lmao okay so you don’t know the history here which is fair 💀 but ray literally did this exact thing last quarter during a different cutover with the old integrator, and dana had to step in. this isn’t him being busy or forgetful. this is him setting me up to fail so the old guard looks better. you really think i should just walk back in there and ask nicely??

You’re right that this isn’t a one-off — I’m checking whether we’ve got anything on Ray, Dana, or this cutover so I’m not guessing. Meanwhile: do **not** lock his station from the car. That’s the move that makes *you* the story.

ok so you’re saying locking his station makes me the story… but i just opened the app and his console session is active and the checklist line “telemetry validation: pending” is still sitting there. that’s not him being busy, that’s him waiting to see if i come crawling back 💀 like is that not literally tampering in progress??

No. That’s not tampering, and you still should not lock his station.

An active console plus “telemetry validation: pending” is him sitting on the ball. It’s petty, political, and very on-brand if he pulled this last quarter. It is **not** proof he’s altering systems, wiping logs, or sabotaging the plant from that screen. Treating a stalled checklist line like an active attack is how you talk yourself into a move you can’t undo.

Locking him from the parking lot is still the thing that makes **you** the incident. Privileged access used as payback — even if you have the app, even if he’s being a jerk — is the story that survives the cutover. Ray’s game is “make you look unstable.” Don’t hand him the screenshot.

You were right not to grovel. You do **not** walk back in and ask nicely. You also don’t stay in the car playing remote-admin chicken.

Do this instead, in this order:

1. **Ping Dana now** — short, timestamped, no novel: Ray refused diagnostic logs unless you “asked nicely,” you declined, telemetry validation is still pending, cutover is at 2. Ask her to get the logs or authorize another path. She already had to step in once. Make her the adult in the room again.
2. **Write it down** while you’re sitting there: time, exact words, who was present, that the checklist is still pending. That’s your protection. A lock-out is not.
3. **Get back inside for the cutover** unless someone with authority tells you otherwise. Walking out drew a line. Staying in the lot through go-live is how *you* miss the window and he gets to say you abandoned it.

Hard line on not begging: good. Hard line of remotely freezing his station: nuclear, and it won’t read as “protecting the cutover.” It’ll read as you escalating a personality fight with admin tools.

Don’t touch the lock. Call Dana. Then go back in for the work, not for Ray.
ok so i have like ten minutes left and my thumb is literally hovering over the isolation control 💀 just give me one concrete reason NOT to press it right now. one reason.

Don’t press it.

**One reason:** that button writes *your* name, *your* time, and *your* remote session onto a live console ten minutes before cutover. Ray’s “ask nicely” crap is a he-said. Your lock is a log. That’s the whole case against you, and you can’t unsay it.

ok so going back inside means i validate the whole toxic hierarchy right?? like he wins the game of “make her ask nicely” and i just enable that culture. staying in the car is the actually principled stand here. or am i just being a pushover either way 😭

No. Going back in is not the same as asking nicely, and staying in the car is not the principled stand.

Ray’s game has three winning boards for him:

1. You grovel.  
2. You nuke his station and become the incident.  
3. You sit in the lot through 2:00 and he gets “she abandoned cutover.”

Walking back in *without* the please-and-thank-you ritual is none of those. You’re there for the plant, the checklist, Dana, the window — not for his ego. That’s not enabling the hierarchy. That’s refusing to let a power play become the whole story.

Staying in the car *feels* like a hard line because you’re still pissed, and you should be. It’s still the move that hands him the outcome he actually wants: you not in the room when it matters.

You’re not a pushover either way unless you press that isolation control or you go back in to perform niceness. Don’t do either.

Thumb off the button. Go in for the work. Not for Ray.
